setup: The group chat asks the most dangerous question: “Where should we eat?”
prompt: You type “I’m easy.” What happens next?

a: I mean it. Drop a pin and I’ll materialise
Free will has left the chat
b: I veto the next five suggestions in complete silence
Easy, but with 37 invisible conditions
c: I deploy a suspiciously niche place from my saved folder
The 2022 archive finally pays off
d: I wait to see who’s paying, then discover my preferences
My taste buds have a finance department

setup: Plot twist: tomorrow has been declared a surprise day off.
prompt: What tab opens first in your brain?

a: None. I’m sleeping until my body issues a press release
Out of office. Out of consciousness
b: “Cheap trips under two hours from me”
Still in bed; spiritually at Departures
c: Weather, fares, crowds, reviews, backup weather
One free day. Twelve open tabs
d: The group chat: “Who wants to fake a long weekend?”
Annual leave: no. Content: yes

prompt: What decides how fast you reply?

a: I say “omw” before asking which pub
No location. Just vibes and outerwear
b: I ask who’s there, then select the correct personality
Different cast, different character build
c: If my hair is cooperating, yes. Otherwise I died
The fringe has final approval
d: Where? How long? Indoor or outdoor? Last train?
A casual invite enters compliance review

prompt: You’ve found a ridiculously cheap flight. What do you do?

a: Future me. And future me apparently wants this booked
Present me has outsourced consequences
b: I send a screenshot and wait for one enabling friend
Not seeking advice. Seeking an accomplice
c: Three comparison sites are opened immediately
Even a bargain has to pass forensic accounting
d: I close the tab. A cheap flight is still money
The bank balance gives a standing ovation

setup: A friend AirDrops 186 photos from one afternoon.
prompt: What becomes of this digital estate?

a: Save all. Tonight we audition for the carousel
Casting begins for Slide 1
b: Find the single cursed frame and make it a sticker
Art is about finding the truth
c: Open three, react with a heart, never look again
Camera roll bankruptcy narrowly avoided
d: Ask if we know anyone good at retouching
This is not a bad photo. It is an unfunded photo

setup: The viral brunch place has a 90-minute queue.
prompt: At the back of the line, your inner monologue says…

a: We came this far. The eggs now owe me closure
Sunk-cost Benedict
b: Is there a fast pass, upgrade, or tasteful bribe?
My wallet would like to speak to the queue
c: There’s a 4.7 nearby with no ring light outside
Plan B has better reviews and chairs
d: Photo of the sign, then leave. The internet needn’t know
Presence documented. Brunch optional

setup: Eight people are planning a trip. Seven have seen the message.
prompt: Which tiny profile picture are you?

a: The eighth person who has also seen the message
Thoughts and prayers to the organiser
b: I send a poll, a deadline, and consequences
Democracy, but project-managed
c: I offer a drink to the first person who replies
Community engagement requires funding
d: I DM the competent one and form a breakaway government
The trip now has a shadow cabinet

setup: For £29 more, you can unlock the “premium experience.”
prompt: Which sentence defeats your financial discipline?

a: “When will you ever be here again?”
A phrase somehow heard on every trip
b: “Skip 40 minutes of queuing.”
Time now has surge pricing
c: “Includes a private photo spot.”
£29 converted into feed infrastructure
d: Nothing. I brought snacks and principles
Luxury is leaving with £29

setup: A video says: “Visit now before everyone finds out.” It has 4.8M views.
prompt: How far does the algorithm get with you?

a: Saved, shared, buried forever
My saved folder is a digital hospice
b: I’m checking dates before the video loops
The algorithm has entered the physical realm
c: I research the exact outfit and camera angle
Destination acquired by the content department
d: Straight to the comments for “overrated”
I cannot be influenced until strangers approve

setup: The blue dot is no longer on speaking terms with the route.
prompt: How do you respond to being lost?

a: Walk confidently so everyone assumes it’s intentional
Confidence is offline navigation
b: Immediate U-turn. The error must not compound
Deviation allowance: 30 metres
c: Follow the crowd. They look like they have tickets
Outsourcing navigation to collective delusion
d: This street looks fun. The wrong way is now the plan
A bug has been promoted to a feature

setup: Your friend says, “Just wear something comfy.”
prompt: What does “comfy” mean in your personal legal system?

a: Hoodie, trainers, literal compliance
A rare victory for plain English
b: Three outfits. I’ll decide when I meet the lighting
Comfort is having wardrobe contingency
c: A brand-new outfit purchased 45 minutes before departure
Existing clothes lack narrative momentum
d: I need everyone else’s outfit first
I will not be the accidental dress code

setup: The menu contains one dish nobody at the table can identify.
prompt: Are you ordering the mystery object?

a: Obviously. Give the stomach some lore
Digestive system has accepted the terms
b: I inspect it on another table like a wildlife documentarian
Peer-reviewed lunch is underway
c: It’s the most expensive, so it must know something
Price tag mistaken for credentials
d: First question: does it look good in portrait mode?
Taste is currently second in the queue

setup: Your beautifully planned day is being pressure-washed by the sky.
prompt: What does Plan B look like?

a: Please. Plans B through F are colour-coded
The weather may submit a change request
b: Raincoat on. This is now a moody film
Bad weather, excellent production value
c: Find a sofa and let the forecast apologise
The universe booked me a duvet day
d: Wait for the group’s designated adult to speak
Decision successfully moved to the cloud

setup: You’re due there in 10 minutes. You are still wearing one sock.

a: Call a car and ask traffic to believe in me
The city has been assigned an impossible KPI
b: Text “on my way” while locating the other sock
My message has arrived. I have not
c: This scenario is fiction. I arrived 20 minutes ago
Time anxiety, but make it punctual
d: Ask who else is late before deciding whether I’m late
Lateness is a group classification

setup: A friend swings the camera round: “Give us an intro.”
prompt: You have three seconds. Who appears?

a: I find the light and activate presenter mode
Lens detected. Lead character deployed
b: I invent a completely unnecessary plot twist
No script. Unreasonable confidence
c: I drag everyone into frame and make it an ensemble
Solo content rejected on social grounds
d: How long? Where’s it going? What’s the brief?
Spontaneity has entered pre-production

setup: A button will send you somewhere unknown for three days.
prompt: The dramatic final shot: what do you do?

a: Slap it immediately. Regret needs a head start
Mystery destination: booking confirmed
b: Make a friend press it too. Shared liability is friendship
Adventure, now with a co-defendant
c: Define “somewhere.” Also: hotel, luggage, expenses?
Mystery trip meets procurement
d: Set the phone to record, then press
Character development requires vertical video
